title: Attention spans and pacing with young children
hook: Six-year-olds can focus on one activity for a short time only. Planning in short chunks keeps them learning.
coreIdeaMd:
A rough guide is a few minutes of focused attention per year of age, so plan in short chunks:

- **Change the activity** every 10 to 15 minutes.
- **Mix sitting and moving.** A quick movement break resets attention.
- **Keep instructions short**: one or two steps at a time, then check.

checkItems.stemMd: How should you give instructions to a Year 1 class?
options: One or two steps at a time, then check
checkItems.answer: One or two steps at a time, then check
checkItems.feedbackCorrect: Yes. Short instructions are easier to follow.
checkItems.feedbackIncorrect: Young students hold only a few steps in mind. Give one or two at a time.
